record_reviews.summary: Swinhoe gives Formosan and Chinese observations: a detailed reported account of dogs punishing a mating pair, a correction to his earlier belief about thrush spurs, and a description of wild and domestic cattle with plans to collect specimens for the Zoological Society.
record_reviews.date_assessment: The header is [before 1 October 1865?], XML 1809-01-01 through 1865-09-30. The question and field reports are later than the requested period on the available bound.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Robert Swinhoe writes; the dog story is explicitly attributed to T. Watters and Chinese informants, and the cattle evidence is Swinhoe’s intended future collection.
record_reviews.unmatched_reason: The letter contains several possible responses to earlier Darwin enquiries but no identifiable prompt or date in this packet.

record_reviews.summary: William Tearle writes after reading Origin, proposing a reconciliation of Genesis with evolution by treating man as previously created as a superior animal; he develops the textual argument across several paragraphs and signs as a humble correspondent.
record_reviews.date_assessment: The header is [before 16 April 1880], XML 1809-01-01 through 1880-04-15. The explicit Origin discussion and broad bound are far later than the period.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: William Tearle is the surviving author; biblical quotations and his speculative theory are his attributed prose.
record_reviews.unmatched_reason: An unsolicited response to Darwin’s published work is present, but no period prompt or receipt is shown.

record_reviews.summary: Darwin asks R. H. Blair for observations of emotional expression in people born blind, especially raised/open hands and shoulder shrugging, and requests permission to quote the evidence in his planned essay.
record_reviews.date_assessment: The header is [before 16 March 1871], XML 1809-01-01 through 1871-03-15. No lower bound supports 1847–1850.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Darwin writes; the enclosed questionnaire and the son’s earlier report are referenced sources, not surviving Blair answers.
record_reviews.unmatched_reason: This is an initiated request for missing observations, with no incoming prompt or response in the packet.

record_reviews.summary: Darwin reports a controlled observation of thirteen marked cobwebs on the Kew Garden hedge, revisiting them with Emma as witness, and argues that the marked webs had not disappeared. He thanks Georgina for the observations that encouraged his Species work.
record_reviews.date_assessment: The mutually exclusive XML alternatives are 1 October in every year 1846–1871. The header is “1 October [1846?–71]”; without a discriminating internal date, the alternatives include 1847–1850 and many later years, so this probe cannot be admitted to the period.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Darwin writes to Georgina Tollet; Emma is an observing witness inside the body, not a co-author.
record_reviews.unmatched_reason: The spider-web observations clearly answer Georgina’s prior account, but no packet prompt is present and the year remains unresolved.

record_reviews.summary: Darwin asks John St Barbe to have his broker identify guaranteed or preference railway shares, prices and conversion rights, and adds an uncertain note about the North Staffordshire guarantee.
record_reviews.date_assessment: The header is [before 3 July 1862], XML 1809-01-01 through 1862-07-02. No lower bound supports period eligibility.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Darwin writes; the broker and railway information are requested third-party material.
record_reviews.unmatched_reason: The investment query initiates a business exchange; no packet source answers it.

record_reviews.summary: The surviving block is an extract from Dr W. D. Hartman’s Pennsylvania journal, dated 6–7 June 1851, beginning with the cicada emergence report. The extract ends mid-sentence, so the source is incomplete.
record_reviews.date_assessment: The header is [before 31 October 1868], XML 1809-01-01 through 1868-10-30; the internal quoted journal dates 1851, but they date the reported observation, not necessarily Darwin’s receipt or the extract’s transmission.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: The block is Hartman’s attributed journal prose; no Darwin or sender voice is established in the surviving fragment and the scholarly section was treated separately.
record_reviews.unmatched_reason: There is no recoverable incoming question, and the fragment’s missing continuation prevents a specific correspondence link.

record_reviews.summary: Darwin’s long memorandum surveys sexual melanism and sexual dimorphism across mammals, birds and other animals, ending with a question about Palamedea and Anseranas as modified goose types. The preserved small skeletal visual was inspected separately; it adds no date or correspondent text.
record_reviews.date_assessment: The header is [before 25 March 1868], XML 1809-01-01 through 1868-03-24. The broad bound cannot establish 1847–1850.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Darwin is the writer; the taxonomic examples are his compiled observations and references, with a preserved visual/enclosure section inspected separately.
record_reviews.unmatched_reason: The closing question seeks an unlocated Huxley or other expert response; no specific incoming prompt survives.

record_reviews.summary: Darwin asks Lucy Wedgwood to inspect Botanical Magazine plate 356 for glutinous Erica Massoni flowers or leaves and glandular hairs, then asks detailed questions about peony pods, colour, birds and fleshy seed coats.
record_reviews.date_assessment: The header is [before 25 September 1866], XML 1809-01-01 through 1866-09-24. No lower bound places it in 1847–1850.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Darwin writes; the book/plate and peony observations are requested external evidence.
record_reviews.unmatched_reason: These are initiated questions, with no incoming source or response in the packet.

record_reviews.summary: Margaret Wedgwood reports counts from 256 Lythrum specimens—94 long-, 95 middle- and 69 short-pistilled—then describes collection difficulties, habitat mixing and finding Hottonia with differently sized pistils.
record_reviews.date_assessment: The header is [before 4 August 1862], XML 1809-01-01 through 1862-08-03. The upper bound and editorial dating do not establish an 1847–1850 date.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Margaret is the writer and reports observations by the Wedgwood party; the separate CD annotations are scholarly apparatus, not her voice.
record_reviews.unmatched_reason: The report likely answers Darwin’s prior Lythrum questions, but the prompt is absent and receipt/composition cannot be dated here.

record_reviews.summary: Darwin’s surviving line praises Lucy Wedgwood’s mother for having two sons who were true naturalists. It is only one body paragraph and lacks the surrounding request or date evidence.
record_reviews.date_assessment: The header is [before 2 June 1876?], XML 1809-01-01 through 1876-06-01. The upper bound is later and no lower bound supports 1847–1850.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Darwin’s single surviving sentence is available, but the fragment’s missing context leaves its recipient and purpose only header-level.
record_reviews.unmatched_reason: The fragment cannot identify an incoming prompt or reply scope.

record_reviews.summary: The surviving cover text lists Comparative Embryology by Balfour and The Brain as an Organ of Mind by Bastian, then asks Darwin to send Semper’s Biology translation when published.
record_reviews.date_assessment: The header is [before 4 September 1880], XML 1809-01-01 through 1880-09-03. The list and publication request do not establish a period date.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Darwin’s brief cover note is readable but detached from the listed books and any incoming letter.
record_reviews.unmatched_reason: No prompt or receipt context survives; the cover fragment is insufficient for a correspondence edge.

record_reviews.summary: Bonavia describes peloric Clitoria Ternatea flowers, sends two imperfect coloured drawings, and classifies six gradations from ordinary to perfectly peloric forms, including stamen fusion/freeing and four-petalled specimens.
record_reviews.date_assessment: The header is [before 7 September 1868], XML 1809-01-01 through 1868-09-06. The source is a later boundary item and has no period-specific lower bound.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Emanuel Bonavia is the surviving author; the native artist’s drawings are an attributed embedded witness and the source remains a fragment.
record_reviews.unmatched_reason: The observations may have been sent in response to Darwin’s botanical interests, but no identifiable question or receipt is present.

record_reviews.summary: Wintle, a volunteer and amateur observer, reports worms emerging during firing drills even on dry common ground, compares soil at Wimbledon and asks Darwin’s view after reading the book on worm mould formation.
record_reviews.date_assessment: The header is [before 9 December 1881], XML 1809-01-01 through 1881-12-08. The explicit reference to Darwin’s published worm book places the context later than 1850.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Douglas J. Wintle is the author; his field observations are firsthand claims and the book is a published work, not a missing letter.
record_reviews.unmatched_reason: The letter is an unsolicited observation/question with no packet antecedent.

record_reviews.summary: Darwin thanks Charles Boner for two works, says he used them in his present book, comments on Tyrolean scenery, and welcomes the reported coexistence of wild varieties and the new wild-boar fact.
record_reviews.date_assessment: The header is [before 8 January 1870], XML 1809-01-01 through 1870-01-07. The explicit present-book context is later than the period.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Darwin writes; Boner’s books and observations are incoming materials described retrospectively, not a period source.
record_reviews.unmatched_reason: The letter answers Boner’s works/letter but no packet antecedent is available and the date is outside the period bounds.

record_reviews.summary: The preserved projection states that the online transcript is unavailable and only summarizes an excerpt concerning Zacharias’s article about Darwin’s objections to Marcus Cohen’s heredity theory.
record_reviews.date_assessment: The header is [before 3 January 1876], XML 1809-01-01 through 1876-01-02. No lower bound or surviving body establishes period eligibility.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: No surviving Darwin prose is available in this record: the catalogue synopsis is not a body and the article’s reported voices cannot be treated as a readable letter.
record_reviews.unmatched_reason: Body unavailable; no historical link can be assessed without source retrieval.

record_reviews.summary: Bornet sends ten cultivated forms of Draba verna following Jordan’s sowing advice, describes a failed Papaver experiment and a sterile dubium × Rhoeas hybrid whose anthers lacked pollen, and thanks Darwin for a previous memoir.
record_reviews.date_assessment: The header is [before 20 August 1867], XML 1809-01-01 through 1867-08-19. Its scientific references and upper bound are later than 1850.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Edouard Bornet writes in French; Jordan’s sowing instructions are quoted/attributed, and the separate scholarly enclosure/annotations were read as apparatus.
record_reviews.unmatched_reason: The thanks identify a prior Darwin memoir, but neither that input nor its receipt date is preserved.

record_reviews.summary: Darwin asks Bosquet for pigeon specimens and authenticated long-distance Carrier flight records, including origins, destinations and distances, and asks that specimens be sent through a bookseller.
record_reviews.date_assessment: The header is [before 3 November 1856], XML 1809-01-01 through 1856-11-02. The broad upper bound is earlier than the period but the source is a boundary probe and has no exact composition day establishing 1847–1850.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Darwin is the surviving writer; the requested carrier information and skins are prospective inputs, not received evidence.
record_reviews.unmatched_reason: This is an initiated request with no incoming prompt or receipt shown; no link is proposed.

issues: These are boundary_date_probe records. Broad before/after and alternative-year constraints were retained; packet membership was not treated as proof of 1847–1850 eligibility. Editorial bibliographies, scholarly sections, original quotations and preserved visual/enclosure material were read as apparatus or attributed evidence, not silently as Darwin voice.
